title: Editor E0 slice: the bundle-byte gate blocks a build that ships CRDT bytes outside the editor
detail:
Split from PROG-E0 on 2026-11-16. PROG-E0B shipped scripts/check-editor-bundle-bytes.mjs advisory (`|| true`, exit 0 on every arm) because it had never read a real artifact. The production build of main then printed it green: 633 routes read, /(main)/pages/canvas/page at 116.6 KB, no route outside the editor named. This row arms it.

WHAT CHANGED. postbuild now runs `node scripts/check-editor-bundle-bytes.mjs` bare, last, chained with &&, so it is the seventh blocking artifact gate. The script's default is blocking: exit 0 clean, exit 1 on a leak (a route outside EDITOR_ROUTES names a chunk that carries yjs or y-prosemirror), exit 79 when it could not look. `--warn-only` is the old advisory mode and a test fails it, or `|| true`, in postbuild as a silent demotion.

COULD NOT LOOK IS A LOUD FAILURE, the convention of the six siblings (build-budget, og-trace, build-fanout and notfound-routes exit non-zero on a missing .next; shell-weight fails on an empty measured set). The arms: no .next, no route manifests, the runtime in no chunk, no manifest matching EDITOR_ROUTES, more manifests unreadable than read, its own crash, and one new arm: no chunk named by any manifest is a file under .next/static. Before this, a compiler upgrade that changed how manifests name chunks would have read as 'every carrier is lazy' and printed green. Two conditions are a loud warning line and not a failure, because a healthy build can produce them: one manifest that will not load (it was skipped silently before; now counted and printed), and an editor route that names no carrier (the canvas moved behind a client-side import). The chunk scan also skips a directory named like a chunk instead of crashing on it.

WHY IT IS SAFE TO ARM. Checked each way it could fail a healthy build: the editor route allowlist is a path regex, and a test reads app/(main)/pages/canvas/page.tsx so a rename fails a test before it fails a build; each fingerprint is proven a literal in the installed package by a test, so an upgrade that drops one fails a test; chunks are matched by hashed basename, which the real reading resolved; a chunk a route manifest names is a chunk that route loads, so a leak is a real finding and not a naming accident; a Vercel preview runs postbuild, so a leak is red on the PR before main. The Space page builder loads lib/editor-crdt through import(), which is counted as lazy, and the real reading confirms it.

VERIFIED: 34 fixture tests, each exit code by running the real script on a fixture tree (clean 0; leak 1; seven cannot-look arms 79; two warning arms 0 with the line printed; --warn-only 0 on leak, missing artifact and crash), and the postbuild pin. The probe fails on origin/main and passes here. NOT VERIFIED: this change on a real build. This box cannot build. The first preview or production build of this branch is the first blocking reading; the new chunks-on-disk arm is satisfied by the reading already taken (the canvas route's chunk resolved to 116.6 KB on disk), but the count of manifests that would not load on a real artifact was never printed before, which is why that condition warns and does not fail below the floor.

ALSO: the PROG-E0B probe required the advisory spelling; that clause is retired there and the blocking wiring is held by this row's probe. Docs: DEPLOY-SAFETY.md rule 13 and its two gate lists, AGENTS.md (seven gates), RUNBOOKS.md (what to do when it fires).

verify.note: Fails on main: postbuild swallows the gate with `|| true` and the script exits 0 on a leak. Passes once postbuild runs the script bare with nothing that can swallow an exit code, AND the script run with no flags exits 1 on a fixture artifact where a public route names a chunk carrying the CRDT runtime (naming route and chunk), exits 0 on the same artifact without that reference, and exits non-zero (not the leak code) with no .next and with manifests whose chunk names resolve to nothing on disk.
